source_caption:
🎬 I, Robot (2004)

I, Robot follows Detective Del Spooner, a Chicago police officer living in the year 2035, when highly advanced robots have become an essential part of everyday life. While most people trust robots to follow strict laws designed to protect humans, Spooner remains deeply suspicious of artificial intelligence. When a brilliant robotics scientist mysteriously dies, Spooner begins investigating a humanoid robot named Sonny, who appears capable of emotions, independent thinking, and possibly even murder. As the investigation unfolds, he uncovers a dangerous conspiracy that threatens humanity’s relationship with technology. With powerful corporations, intelligent machines, and unexpected enemies standing in his way, Spooner must uncover the truth before it’s too late. Combining thrilling action, futuristic technology, and thought-provoking storytelling, the film explores artificial intelligence, free will, trust, and the dangers of technological advancement.

🎭 Genre: Sci-Fi • Action • Mystery • Thriller

⭐ IMDb: 7.1/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 55m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Alex Proyas

🏆 Recognition: Starring Will Smith, Bridget Moynahan, and Alan Tudyk, the film earned over $350 million worldwide and received an Academy Award nomination for Best Visual Effects. Inspired by the works of Isaac Asimov, it became a memorable science-fiction blockbuster exploring humanity’s relationship with intelligent machines.

source_details.synopsis: I, Robot (sometimes stylized as i,Robot) is a 2004 American science fiction action film directed by Alex Proyas, from a screenplay by Jeff Vintar and Akiva Goldsman. It stars Will Smith, Bridget Moynahan, Bruce Greenwood, James Cromwell, Chi McBride, and Alan Tudyk. The film is named after Isaac Asimov's 1950 short-story collection and incorporates Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics and several characters, though it is not a direct adaptation. The film is set in Chicago in 2035. Highly intelligent robots fill public service positions throughout the world, operating under the Three Laws of Robotics to keep humans safe.
